title: Osho on Meditation for People Who Cannot Sit Still
description: What Osho taught about meditation for restless people, in plain words. If you have ever closed your eyes to meditate and found the whole marketplace rushing in, this one is for you. The drunken monkey of the mind, a child who dances until he falls asleep, the archer who stopped aiming, and the monk who was told to wash his bowl. Then a meditation to shake out the day and fall into stillness.

chapters.title: Osho on Meditation for People Who Cannot Sit Still
chapters.ref: Osho, Walking in Zen, Sitting in Zen

beats.say: You have tried it, haven't you? You sat down, you closed your eyes, you decided to be silent... and within one minute the whole marketplace came rushing in.
Your legs began to ache. You remembered the electricity bill. You remembered something your mother said twenty years ago. And you thought: meditation is not for me.
Osho saw this clearly. Meditation is for you, but perhaps not in the way you were told. You were told to sit still. Nobody told you that first you have to get tired of moving.
He said of meditation: "You have to sit in it, you have to walk in it. Yes, you have even to sleep in it." So tonight we start from where you are. Restless, busy. That restlessness is the door.
In India they say the mind is like a monkey. Not an ordinary monkey... a monkey who has drunk wine. And then a scorpion has stung him.
Imagine this monkey jumping from branch to branch, screaming, never resting for one moment. This is the mind you are asking to sit quietly.
You can't order it. You can't force it. The more you fight the monkey, the wilder it becomes. Every fight gives it more energy.
So the old masters found a strange trick. Let the monkey jump. Let it jump as much as it wants... and you just watch it, with a little smile.
After some time the monkey gets tired. Nobody is fighting it, nobody is chasing it. And a tired monkey sits down by itself.
That is the whole secret of Osho's active meditations. Not control. Tiredness, and then watching. Let the energy move first... and the stillness comes on its own, like evening after a long hot day.
Look at a small child. He cannot sit still for two minutes. He runs, he jumps, he shouts. And then suddenly he falls asleep in the middle of his play.
The child knows something we have forgotten. When the energy has moved, the body rests. You cannot rest a body that has never moved.
So before you sit, dance. Close the door of your room, put some music on the radio, and dance. Not to look beautiful. Nobody is watching. Dance like a madman.
Let the body shake. Let it jump. Let all the tension of the office and the marketplace come out through the hands and the feet.
Then, when you are tired, stop. Suddenly. Sit down on the floor and close your eyes. And now see... how silent it is inside.
This is why Osho's meditations so often begin with dancing. The dance has cleaned the house. Now the guest can come. Silence is the guest... and it only comes to a house that is empty and clean.
There was once a great archer, the best in the whole kingdom. He could split one arrow with another. And he was very proud of it.
One day he went to an old master and said: Look at my skill. The old man watched him shoot, and said: Yes, this is the art of shooting. But it is not yet the art of not shooting.
Then the old man took him up a mountain, to the edge of a cliff above a terrible drop, and stood there on one foot, looking down, perfectly at ease.
Come, he said. Shoot from here. The great archer came to the edge and looked down... and his legs began to tremble. He fell to the ground, sweating.
The old man laughed gently. Your skill is in your hands, he said. But your mind is full of fear. A man who is truly at ease does not need to aim. He hits.
Osho taught: tension is not concentration. The more you try, the more you miss. Relax... and you will be surprised how much happens through you.
If you cannot sit, walk. The Buddha's monks did it for hours. Slowly, up and down, in the morning before the sun came up.
Feel the left foot touching the earth. Then the right foot. Left... right. Not thinking about the feet. Feeling them.
Walk so slowly that the mind gets bored and goes away. Each step is complete in itself. You are not going anywhere. You have already arrived.
You can do it on the way to the bus stop. You can do it in the long corridor of your office. Nobody needs to know. It is your secret.
And one day you will notice that the walking is happening, and you are only watching it. The body walks... and you are still.
Osho taught that this stillness in the middle of movement is the real meditation. It is not in the sitting. It is in the watching.

chapters.title: Then Wash Your Bowl
chapters.ref: A Zen story · Osho, Hyakujo: The Everest of Zen

beats.say: A new monk came to the monastery and said to the master: I have just arrived. Please, teach me.
The master asked: Have you eaten your breakfast? Yes, said the monk. Then go and wash your bowl, said the master. And the monk understood.
It sounds like nothing. Wash your bowl. But listen... the master is saying: Don't ask for something special. Do what is in front of you, totally.
The restless mind always wants the next thing, the big thing, the spiritual thing. And the bowl is sitting there, dirty, waiting for you.
Osho said: "Any mundane activity can become meditative." Wash the bowl with your whole being. And you will find that the temple was always in the kitchen.
Here is one more way for the restless ones. Close your lips, and hum. Like a bee. Not loud. Just enough to feel it inside.
Let the humming fill your head, your chest, your belly. After some time you will feel that you are not humming... the humming is happening.
The mind cannot think and hum at the same time. Try it. The thoughts become fewer and fewer, because the energy is going into the sound.
Then stop. And in the moment after the sound, listen. The silence will be so alive... you can almost touch it.
Osho made humming into a whole meditation, Nadabrahma. Sound is a boat. Silence is the other shore. Use the boat... and then leave it on the bank.
And let me tell you something strange. The restless ones are lucky. A man who is lazy and dull has very little energy to go inwards. You have plenty.
Energy is energy. The same energy that runs after money and fame can turn around and run inwards. It is like a river changing its direction.
The priests told you to kill your restlessness. Don't kill it. Use it. Ride it, like a horse, until it carries you home.
A dead horse goes nowhere. A wild horse, once it trusts you, can take you to the farthest mountain.
Osho never asked anyone to be ashamed of restlessness. It is not a disease. It is a thirst... and thirst is the beginning of every search.

chapters.title: A Meditation: Shake, Then Be Still

beats.say: Now let us try something in the spirit of Osho's Kundalini meditation. Stand up, if you can. Let your arms hang loose. And close your eyes.
Begin to shake. Start with the hands. Then let the shaking go into the arms, the shoulders, the whole body. Don't do it. Let it happen.
Shake out the whole day. The bus, the boss, the quarrel, the worry. Let it all fall off you, like dust from an old coat.
Now... slowly... let the shaking become smaller. And smaller. And stop. Stand completely still.
Sit down. Feel the body tingling, alive. Feel the breath, still fast, slowly becoming calm. Don't do anything to it.
This is the stillness you could not find before. It was waiting behind the restlessness. You only had to go through it.
Rest here for a while. Nothing to achieve. Nothing to become. Only this breath... and the next.
And when you are ready, open your eyes... slowly. Take this stillness with you into your day. Good night, my friend.
